title: Other Deployment Options
description: Deploy Next.js anywhere: Node.js server, Docker, AWS, Netlify, or static export.

slides.title: You're Not Locked In 🗝️
slides.content:
# Beyond Vercel

Next.js is a standard Node.js application. You can deploy it anywhere that runs Node.js.

Options:

* **Self‑hosted Node.js** – run `npm start` behind a reverse proxy (Nginx).
* **Docker** – containerize your app.
* **AWS / Google Cloud / Azure** – use their compute services.
* **Netlify** – native Next.js support via Essential Next.js plugin.
* **Static Export** – if your app is fully static (no SSR/API routes).

Next.js gives you flexibility.

slides.title: Docker Deployment 🐳
slides.content:
# Containerize Next.js

Next.js provides an official Docker image and sample Dockerfile.

```dockerfile
FROM node:18-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production
COPY . .
RUN npm run build
CMD ["npm", "start"]
```

Or use `output: 'standalone'` in `next.config.js` for a smaller image:

```js
module.exports = { output: 'standalone' };
```

This produces a self‑contained `.next/standalone` folder that includes only the necessary files.

quizData.question: What does the `output: 'standalone'` option do?

options.text: It makes the app run without a server
It creates a self‑contained build with only necessary dependencies, perfect for Docker

quizData.explanation: `standalone` mode bundles only the files needed to run, omitting dev dependencies and source files, resulting in a smaller production image.

slides.title: Deploying to a VPS (Node.js + PM2) 💻
slides.content:
# Traditional Hosting

You can deploy to a Linux server with Nginx as a reverse proxy and PM2 to manage the Node.js process.

1. Clone your repo, run `npm install`, `npm run build`.
2. Use PM2: `pm2 start npm --name "next-app" -- start`.
3. Configure Nginx to proxy `localhost:3000`.

This gives you full control, but you must handle SSL, monitoring, and scaling yourself.

slides.title: PM2 Start (Terminal)
slides.content: Keep the Next.js server alive across reboots.
slides.codeSnippet:
npm install -g pm2
pm2 start npm --name "next-app" -- start
pm2 save
pm2 startup

slides.title: Netlify & Static Export 🌐
slides.content:
# Netlify

Netlify has an **Essential Next.js** plugin that automatically detects Next.js and configures serverless functions for SSR/API routes. You just connect your repo.

# Static Export

If your app uses only `getStaticProps` and no API routes, you can export static HTML:

```bash
next build && next export
```

This creates an `out` folder that you can host on any static hosting (S3, GitHub Pages).

**Limitation:** No SSR, ISR, API routes, or middleware.

quizData.question: When can you use `next export`?

options.text: When your app is fully static (no SSR, no API routes, no middleware)
Always, it's an alternative to `npm start`

quizData.explanation: `next export` turns your app into a static site. It only works if every page can be rendered at build time without a server.

slides.title: Cloud Providers 🏢
slides.content: AWS Amplify, Google Cloud Run, and Azure Static Web Apps all have guides for Next.js. Many use a combination of CloudFront/CDN + Lambda or their own serverless offerings. Choose based on your existing infrastructure.
